¶3 Now there is one definition of Aarif by Amirul Momineen (as) which is, I think one of the most beautiful description of a mystic so to speak, he said “the knower he's the one who knows his soul and frees it and purifies it and whatever keeps it at bay”. Now, first of all, he knows his soul or his self. Secondly, the self is settled by some sort of chain which is just making it bound to the Earth to the body and Aarif is the one who frees that self and then purifies it the thing is to purify it so that it could move, move up, purified from whatever keeps it at bay, keep it a distance from Allah (swt).

¶4 We are at distance with Allah because, of course, the police force in this world wouldn't allow us to enter that holy height of presence of Allah (swt),I usually when I recite this ayat about Jahannam and that Allah is shadeedul eqaab. I imagine like this, that this world you say a society needs the police force. If there is no police force, everything goes into, the whole creation needs a police and that's the police force of Allah(swt) who keeps everything in order, and punishes those who want to somehow violate otherwise would have ended up would have been ended up in a mess .Especially on the Day of Judgment we might see that if there is not that punishment is not there, if that justice is not there, the whole creation of Allah (swt) would be destroyed.

¶5 So that police force, that utmost justice keeps us at distance from Allah (swt) unless we prepare for it, just like just imagine it's just like the house of a State President that the police wouldn't let you get it unless you have some permission. You have some qualification. You have some appointment. With Allah (swt) of course there's no such an appointment needed. No actual authorities needed only purification you have to purify, to be able to enter into that holy site, so the Aarif is the one who keeps his soul pure from whatever keeps it away from Allah (swt).

¶6 Now this was just a definition of Aarif so by this definition we know what we are leaving what is involved in our hearts, knowing the self, freeing it from desire, purifying it so that it could move towards Allah. And, of course, entering the holy side the holy precinct of Allah(swt).

¶7 Now, usually the mystics have a terminology for themselves, certainly any knowledge if you want to communicate to other for that knowledge it had its own terminology the mystics have their own terminology which is often taken from some hadees from the Prophet(pbuh) they say, We don't only have Sharia, Sharia is the very outward shell of religion. There is Sharia the law and this Sharia is confirming the injunctions of the Prophet and practicing them. This is called Sharia, the law. Okay. So what usually we are dealing with in religion is Sharia, we want to know, how should we pray, when should we pray, how should we fast when should we fast? What are the perquisites of prayer?

¶8 What are the prequisites of fasting? These are all things that we want to know and then we want to track, Okay, so this is Sharia. Now then there is of course, we don't do all these things for themselves. We do it for something else. We want to gain something we want to go somewhere. And in fact that place that we want to go is the vicinity of Allah(swt). So we want to move from one place to another place. So the Sharia is not done for its own sake, Sharia is done for something else. So there is a path from Sharia to that very thing which we want to go to, which is called tareeqa, it literally means path.

¶9 Now the Sufi tareeqas that you have heard most probably is only the systematization of this path which goes from Sharia theology. So tareeqa is realizing the manners and attitudes of the Prophet in one own self. This is what they called as tareeqa. Sharia is the outward appearance of the law. Prophet did the same salaat as we do but did he get the same meaning as we did he find the same meaning in salaat and we certainly the salaat of the Prophet was different from our salaat. Although if for example, if you sit there, and Prophet is here, and we are here and we pray together, a jury is watching and we imitate the Prophet, exactly the same in the same way.

¶10 The jurists will say both salaat are correct. Okay, this is what jurists can say. However, the deeper concepts he cannot realize, he does not know what goes in the heart of the Prophet what goes in our hearts it is what is called tariqa. Now that tariqa should lead us to somewhere and that is Haqiqa which is the truth becoming like the Prophet and seeing what they see. So, the mystiques the real orafa what we are talking from now on, we are talking about the orafa who are acceptable, especially according to Shiah tradition, we can have lots of Sunni orafa of course.

I know other people don't know, other people are just like animals and Allah himself described them in the Quran ‘olaaeka kal alanaam’(sura 7:ayat 179) they are like animals they don’t know anything , Allah favors this knowledge.

¶51 So the beginning of this knowledge is pretention, is claiming about many things that we don't know. Whoever attains the second step become humble and low. Now, they know about God thing which whenever they evoked in their heart, they break down completely, they become humble. And whoever gets to the service, whoever gets to this…… become indigenous towards Allah and feels the need of this verse, yaaa ayyunhan naasu antumul fuqaraaa'u (sura 35: ayat 15).

¶52 O you people you are indigent towards Allah (swt). And of course, and I highly would know that he does not know those who are very close to Allah, they know what their limit of human knowledge towards Allah (swt), now we were talking about tariqa this is going to become a bit disappointing because you want to move through tariqa to reach to haqiqa to know that you know nothing you cannot know anything about Allah (swt), this is the position when the Prophet(pbuh), he used to say ,” you are not………(54:15) you cannot say it is not human capacity, of course I'm just say what ‘Qaaloo subhaanaka laa 'ilma lanaaa illaa maa 'allamtanaaa ( sura 2:32), you have no knowledge but very little knowledge about and this is the end of this knowledge now you might say okay.

¶53 Well, you come at the end to this point. No. And, of course, this is different from what is usually reported from Abu Bakr by ibne arabi, usually quotes Hadith from Abu Bakr. I don't know in what situation abu Baqr has said this. He abu baqr said confessing to one's ignorance is knowledge, its true. And he says this is a position. Ibne Arabi says this is a position so that Abu Bakr says confessing towards ignorance is knowledge in itself. Then, of course, ibne arabi says but among the companions is someone who had no ignorance whatsoever, and that was Ali and the position of Ali is much higher than abu baqr. But when he said he had no ignorance, he meant in the human capacity.

¶54 But there are things beyond him. Which of course, no one can know. Now, he says anytime any possibility that might know God, the way he deserves to be know otherwise God would have been limited. So, you don't think that when you enter jannah alhamdulillah you are now, you now know everything whatever you want, is it not that's just the beginning of the path, beginning of knowing Allah (swt) and then you move forward. Well, with one exception, there you move forward to pleasure, joy, knowing that this has no end whatsoever and you are going to closer and closer and closer and closer, know more and more and more. And this knowledge is very pleasurable. You see mystics they then they like to just get a dream.

¶55 Now in jannah we have every morning and every evening you have a window open to you about a new knowledge new, new unveiling of Allah (swt) for you in a new form. In a way that you will never have contemplated before or never could know before. The jannah is not a place where you eat and merry and enjoy the Gardens and Rivers. No, this is the….. where everyone can… now why this is more described more about jannah than other things rather than other things. Now, we were considering what we have mentioned now, do you know the answer why, if this is not the most important thing of the jannah, why this is the most conspicuous description of the jannah because most people are ahlu Sharia isn't, they only know the sharia they all know the shart and they can only understand the business the reward.

¶56 Okay, if you do this, you get this, you get a glimpse of God , ok ,who wants a glimpse of God, give me a houri or a garden or a palace that I have worked for. What is it a glimpse of God what I want to do with a glimpse of God?

¶57 Taqwa has different depths of course. And you have the outward of course framework of taqwa, which is people of Sharia who perform these duties the Sharia Okay, they are muttaqeen. Actually Quran says ‘hudal lill muttaqeen’ It means it takes you deep because you have to have Taqwa initially. Then you ride on this and go if you don't have taqwa it is not working for you. Certainly, so Quran wants to take us in our taqwa you know, and then of course go in deeper with what how many of muslemeen really can recite Quran knowing its meaning , not the majority ,they recite the Quran they get their reward, no doubt about it. It doesn't mean that when they go to jannah, they don't get those places of God they get it, although they don't want it, although they are not thinking about it.

People of the lower jannah they never can never ever can realize what type of favor or nemat is given to people on the higher. It's not contemplated it is not possible for them to know. ¶59 Well, ashaabul yameen they are on the boundaries certainly, someone who performs Sharia is ashaabul yameen okay, now, they might come to some way into tariqa okay, and still they could be regarded as ashaabul yameen. Then there is a clear criterion and boundry that is a passage then they will come from muqarraboon of course the lowest level of muqarraboon, but that is a very difficult level to attain, to move from this station of ashaabul yameen to station on muqarraboon needs a complete change of attitudes, complete change of outlook towards life. And of course, complete change of desires, willingness and all these things. And this is the meaning of the verse of Sura Nahl ‘Man 'amila saaliham min zakarin aw unsaa wa huwa mu'minun(ayat 97), you have to be momin initially , okay, this ashaabul yameen ok , then you do persistence, okay.

¶60 Then Allah will give you a new life. This new life of muqarraboon , falanuhyiyannahoo hayaatan taiiyibatanw, we give them a pure life, pure life means a life not adultered mixed with lowly desires of this world and then zaaleka fadhlullaahe yu’ti maiyasha, only the Grace of Allah (swt), we cannot attain by our own effort. Of course we need that effort to prepare ourselves for that grace, when the grace comes and of course it will….

No, of course because you are all the time close closer and closer to Allah (swt) and then you gain more knowledge. And this is what actually Allah tells the Prophet. If you want something from God, want more knowledge? Waqur rabbe zidni ilm( sura20: 114) increase my knowledge and increasing the knowledge means moving through this wonder world of Allah(swt) in a way that we describe inshallah later. I think I mentioned this before that once by Aziz, the great mystic whose silsala goes back to Imame Raza (as) he was making ablution and suddenly his disciples went into prostration, saying, subhan rabbiyal azeeme ,he said, what has happened?
